study_identification_part.si4_title: Using normative modeling to assess pharmacological treatment effect on brain state in patients with schizophrenia

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states the aims and the purpose of applying normative modeling. It specifies three objectives: (i) build normative brain aging trajectories from Cam-CAN rs-fMRI, (ii) test whether deviations relate to psychiatric symptoms by decomposing PANSS into 5 factors, and (iii) investigate pharmacological treatment effects on deviation distributions and predict deviation changes from baseline clinical variables.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "this investigation aimed: (i) to use the Cambridge Centre for Ageing and Neuroscience (Cam-CAN) data set to build brain aging trajectories inferred from normative modelsof functional MRI data; (ii) to establish the brain-behaviors relationships, decompose the symptoms into 5 dimensions to test whether deviations from these models were related to psychiatric symptoms in patients with schizophrenia; (iii) to further investigated the pharmacological treatment effect on deviation distributions, and predict the deviation changes using baseline clinical variables."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model using the Cam-CAN healthy cohort and reports the data source, sample size (n=652), ethics, and that scanner parameters and demographics are in the Supplement. However, explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria and imaging QC standards for the Cam-CAN subset used here, and detailed exclusion reasons, are not described in the main text available in this folder.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Data used in the preparation of this work were obtained from the Cam-CAN repository ... (n = 652). ... The demographic characteristics of the sample are described in Table S1. The scanner parameters were also reported in the Supplementary Materials."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Covariates age and sex are incorporated directly into the normative modeling via sex-specific normative age models. Additionally, downstream analyses include sex, age, and head motion as covariates in permutation-based correlations.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "The sex-specific normative age models for each dynamic FC feature were built based on Cam-CAN"; "We used permutation tests (n = 5,000) ... with sex, age, and head motion as covariates."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The data source for the reference cohort is clearly specified as Cam-CAN, with URL and citations, and the sample size is reported.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "Data used in the preparation of this work were obtained from the Cam-CAN repository (available at http://www.mrc-cbu.cam.ac.uk/datasets/camcan/) (Shafto et al. 2014; Taylor et al. 2017) (n = 652)."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Per guide, for SECONDARY data (existing datasets) used as the reference cohort (Cam-CAN), image acquisition protocol assessment is not applicable. The Cam-CAN acquisition parameters are referenced as being in the Supplement.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "The Cam-CAN data set provides detailed imaging data acquisition parameters, we also added this information to the Supplementary Materials."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: The main text in this folder does not describe preprocessing software, pipelines, or QC procedures for the reference cohort data or derived FC features. While analysis steps (atlas, sliding window) are presented, preprocessing details are absent in the available materials (likely in Supplement, not present here).
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: No explicit mention of preprocessing software (e.g., fMRIPrep/SPM/FSL), steps, or QC is found in Lin2024.pdf.md.

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The normative models were estimated under 10-fold cross-validation on healthy individuals (Cam-CAN). They also aggregated 10 models and computed certainty measures based on cross-validated Z-scores.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "...we estimated the normative models of healthy individuals from Cam-CAN under 10-fold cross-validation... Finally, 10 models were aggregated into normative models for dynamic FC features."; "We adopted a certainty measure to evaluate the deviation reliability for each subject based on the 10-fold cross-validation normative model."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset beyond Cam-CAN is described.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No external healthy validation dataset beyond Cam-CAN is reported.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The modeling approach is described: sex-specific normative age models estimated from Cam-CAN using quantile linear regression to derive 5th, 50th, and 95th percentile curves and Z-scores scaled by the 5–95% range. Key settings (percentiles, cross-validation, aggregation) are provided.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "We used quantile linear regression to estimate the normative range... estimate the 50th (median) percentile ... 5th and 95th percentiles..."; "The sex-specific normative age models for each dynamic FC feature were built based on Cam-CAN..."; "Finally, 10 models were aggregated into normative models for dynamic FC features."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: They report quantitative performance metrics for the reference cohort normative model: proportions of supra/infra deviations close to nominal 5% tails and a normative certainty index near 0.99 across features, indicating reliability.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "the proportion of healthy individuals with supra-deviation ... was 2.75% for the aFCS features, and 2.91% for fFCS ... infra-deviation ... 2.82% and 2.92% ... The normative certainty ... average certainty ... 0.991 for aFCS and 0.990 for fFCS"

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: Although 10-fold cross-validation is described, sample sizes per partition and demographic characteristics for each fold/partition are not reported.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: No per-partition (train/validation/test or per-fold) sample sizes or demographics are provided.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and library versions and availability of code/trained models are not reported in the materials available here. While the data source (Cam-CAN) is cited, reproducibility details for the modeling implementation are absent.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: No software/library versions or code/model availability statements are found.

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection: ethics approvals, recruitment numbers for patients and HCs, treatment duration, and dropout counts are reported. However, specific diagnostic inclusion/exclusion criteria and imaging QC standards are not detailed in the main text here.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The Ethics Committee of the Peking University Sixth Hospital approved the study. Forty healthy subjects and 42 patients with schizophrenia were enrolled ... Five patients discontinued ... For the following data analysis, 37 subjects ... The symptom severity ... was evaluated using the PANSS before and after the treatment ... All the patients received mono- or dual-therapy with antipsychotic medications for 6 wk."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses of deviation scores included clinical covariates beyond demographics: PANSS symptom dimensions were modeled via GLMs/correlations, and permutation tests included sex, age, and head motion as covariates.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "General linear models and Pearson's correlations of the deviation profiles on bSCZ/aSCZ and clinical PANSS scores were conducted... We used permutation tests (n = 5,000) ... with sex, age, and head motion as covariates."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary data collection site and scanner are described (Siemens Magnetom Trio 3T at Peking University Third Hospital), but the time period is not provided in the available text.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "Magnetic resonance imaging was performed using a Siemens Magnetom Trio 3.0 Tesla imaging system ... at Peking University Third Hospital."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes and demographic/clinical characteristics are reported, including age, sex, education, age of onset, illness duration, and PANSS subscores at baseline and week 6 (Table 1).
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: Table 1 excerpt shows age, sex, education, age of onset, duration, and PANSS scores (week 0 and week 6).

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: Clinical assessment uses PANSS, with a specified 5-factor model. Assessments were conducted before and after treatment by the same psychiatrist.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "The symptom severity of all schizophrenia patients was evaluated using the PANSS before and after the treatment by the same psychiatrist."; "a 5-factor consensus model of the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale (PANSS)... we adopted this 5-factor model."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: Deviation Z-scores are defined relative to normative percentile curves, and clinical implications are discussed (e.g., networks more likely to return to normal ranges; relationships with symptom dimensions). However, explicit quantitative thresholds to define categories (e.g., |Z| > 1.96) are not specified in the available text.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "...patients' features of the same age were positioned on the normative models to estimate individual deviation Z-scores."; "These results suggested that, the brain networks of those patients with milder depressive symptoms were more likely to be placed back to the normal range in clinical therapy."
